title: US OMB Memo M-24-10 Federal AI Governance — Agency Deadlines, Minimum Practices, and What Comes After December 2026
context: 2026-08-28 engine cycle — OMB M-24-10 (March 2024) required agencies to stand up CAIOs, publish AI use-case inventories, and implement minimum safety practices by December 1, 2024; the next wave of deadlines hits through 2026, and the incoming administration inherits every compliance clock
body: OMB Memorandum M-24-10 (March 28, 2024) is the US federal government's first comprehensive AI governance directive, issued under the Advancing American AI Act and Executive Order 14110. It binds every CFO Act agency and creates a compliance architecture that outlasts any single administration. The key deadlines that matter for providers and auditors in August 2026: (1) Agency CAIOs were required by May 27, 2024 — every major federal agency now has a chief AI officer, and that CAIO carries the sign-off authority for AI use-case inventories and risk determinations. (2) Public AI use-case inventories went live December 1, 2024 and must be updated annually — the 2025 update cycle closed and the 2026 update cycle is now open. Any agency AI system classified as safety-impacting or rights-impacting must be flagged in that inventory, and the flag triggers minimum practice requirements. (3) Minimum safety practices for safety-impacting and rights-impacting AI were required by December 1, 2024 — these include real-world testing, ongoing monitoring, human review of AI outputs, risk assessment, notice and contestation rights for the public, and periodic reporting. If an agency cannot meet a minimum practice, it must document a written waiver approved by the CAIO, and that waiver is public. (4) AI code inventories were required by August 1, 2024 and must be maintained — models, training data, evaluation results, and decision logic must be catalogued. (5) Procurement AI clauses: by March 28, 2025, agencies must include AI-specific terms in contracts covering model access, data rights, evaluation results, and incident reporting. (6) The 150-day deadline for removing non-compliant AI from operations passed in August 2024 — any AI system that could not meet minimum practices was to be retired or brought into compliance. The incoming administration's transition does not pause any of these deadlines; an incoming CAIO inherits the inventory and any open findings. The Council of AI maps M-24-10 directly to measured containment: a minimum-practice requirement to 'conduct ongoing monitoring' is not satisfied by a dashboard screenshot — it is satisfied by a signed measurement stream showing the monitoring check running on a documented schedule, with deviation events traceable to the Containment Incident Index. Concretely for providers selling AI into the federal market: (a) structure your compliance package around the exact M-24-10 minimum-practice checklist — if you cannot show real-world testing results, a written waiver is the only alternative; (b) map each minimum practice to a measurement axis and produce a signed credential per practice on a fixed schedule; (c) file your code inventory against the OMB code-inventory schema, linking model versions to evaluation results; (d) expect agency procurement officers to demand access to your training data schema and evaluation log as a condition of award — the Council of AI publishes an OSCAL-mapped M-24-10 compliance template that maps each minimum practice to a signable measurement.
